hearings, meetings and other relevant activities, including interpretation,travel and accessibility arrangements.Shared working methods: Strengthen procedures for survivor engagement and securecase management, working with colleagues across programs to ensure continuity andavoid unnecessary duplication of requests to survivors.What you bring Relevant practical experience working directly with people on the move, includingthose at risk or in insecure environments, and/or survivors of serious human rightsviolations, including sustained responsibility for individual cases and follow-up Demonstrated experience conducting trauma-informed interviews and documentingsensitive accounts for legal proceedings, human rights investigations or comparablepurposes A basic understanding of legal procedures and avenues for survivors’ access to justiceand participation, together with the ability to acquire detailed procedural knowledge andexplain complex information clearly Strong case management and organizational skills, including reliable documentation,coordination of multiple cases and consistent follow-through Practical understanding of survivor-centred approaches, including respect for individualautonomy, informed and ongoing consent, confidentiality and the right to declineparticipation Sound judgment concerning communication and security risks, including when workingremotely with people in precarious or changing circumstances Experience communicating across languages and working effectively with interpreters,including through telephone calls and messaging applications A commitment to working in partnership with survivor-led organizations andrecognizing survivors’ expertise and role in shaping accountability efforts An intersectional, power-critical approach: an understanding of how racism, gender,nationality, migration status, class, disability and other intersecting structures ofdiscrimination shape experiences of violence and barriers to justice Strong interpersonal skills, a collaborative approach while also able to workindependently, and the ability to build trusting relationships, maintain professionalboundaries and seek specialist input when needed Excellent spoken and written English Willingness to travel occasionally within and outside EuropeA law degree or professional legal qualification is an asset but not required. We welcomerelevant experience gained through professional, community-based and survivor-led work,alongside different educational and professional pathways.The following would be particularly valuable: Arabic language skills, particularly familiarity with Sudanese Arabic, would be asignificant asset. Other languages relevant to the communities we work with, includingFrench, Tigrinya, Amharic, Somali and Mandinka, are also welcome. Experience supporting survivor participation before the ICC, national criminal courts orregional and international human rights mechanisms Familiarity with the Central Mediterranean context, Libya, European borderexternalization or related accountability work Experience coordinating interpreters, interview teams or referral networksWe welcome applications from people of all cultures, backgrounds and experiences. jobs.occupation: Veterinarian (m/f/d) for our Veterinary Laboratory (Tierarzt/-ärztin - Groß- und Nutztiere)
jobs.description: ... part-time or full-timeMicroscopy, counting cells, solving challenging questions and identifying hidden pathogens: In our veterinary laboratory, you will make an important contribution to rapid diagnostics and, therefore, to providing our animal patients with the best possible care. As a veterinarian working alongside your doctoral position at another institution, you will work closely with our team, stay closely connected to the clinical environment and gain exciting insights into diagnoses and treatment courses. As rapid results are often essential in a clinical setting, you will also keep a cool head in demanding situations.If you are driven by a spirit of scientific curiosity, value precise work, would like to help animals and want to enrich our laboratory team with your veterinary expertise, we look forward to receiving your application for our in-house laboratory.Working in our laboratory offers you, as a veterinarian completing the professional recognition period, the opportunity to specifically apply the veterinary knowledge you have already acquired in the field of laboratory diagnostics while gaining an in-depth insight into clinical diagnostics and the resulting treatment decisions. You will work closely with experienced veterinarians and gain first-hand experience of how laboratory findings contribute to the assessment and care of our patients.The position is particularly aimed at veterinarians who have already completed their degree, have gained initial practical experience in veterinary laboratory diagnostics and would like to combine a position in our laboratory with their ongoing doctoral research at another institution for at least 12 months. In this role, you will combine your doctoral position with a professionally demanding position and have the opportunity to continuously deepen your knowledge in hematology, clinical chemistry, cytology, microscopy and other areas of laboratory diagnostics.Our modern laboratory enables comprehensive and rapid diagnostics around the clock, including at night and on weekends. Many test results are available within just 15 to 30 minutes and can be used immediately for diagnostics, treatment and intensive care.Our diagnostic spectrum includes, among other things, hematological and clinical chemistry analyses, blood gas and coagulation analyses, urinalyses, as well as rapid tests for infectious diseases and hormone determinations. Another focus is the microscopic examination and assessment of blood, urine and fecal samples, as well as cytological diagnostics of body cavity effusions, fine-needle aspirates and joint aspirates. In particular, intraoperative rapid diagnostics often help enable well-founded treatment decisions to be made promptly.Your Profile- You have successfully completed your degree in Veterinary Medicine and are currently pursuing a doctoral degree at another institution.- You would like to work in our veterinary laboratory for at least 12 months alongside your doctoral position and gain extensive experience in clinical laboratory diagnostics.- Ideally, you have initial practical experience in veterinary laboratory diagnostics, microscopy or sample processing.- You are interested in hematological, clinical chemistry and cytological questions and enjoy carefully assessing findings and identifying diagnostic connections.- You work precisely, independently and responsibly and are able to maintain an overview even when handling a high volume of samples and time-critical examinations.- You enjoy working closely with experienced veterinarians and our entire laboratory team.- Good German skills are an advantage, but are not a prerequisite. Very good English skills at C1 level are equally welcome for this position.- You enjoy further developing your veterinary knowledge in a clinical setting and learning about the connection between laboratory findings, diagnostics and treatment.Your Responsibilities- Analysis of a wide range of samples from our outpatient and inpatient patients- Performing and assessing laboratory diagnostic examinations as part of our in-house diagnostics- Microscopy: differential blood count including staining, ear cytology and urine sediment examination- Performing and assessing specialized examinations such as body cavity effusion analysis, synovial fluid analysis and platelet assessment- Assessing and interpreting laboratory findings in close collaboration with our medical team- Supporting the timely provision and interpretation of findings for diagnostics, treatment and intensive care- Collaboration with and shipment of samples to external laboratories (IDEXX, Antech, Laboklin and others)- Ordering of consumables and laboratory supplies- Billing of examinations and external services in Vetera- Close collaboration with our medical team and gaining insight into clinical decision-making processes- Communication with pet owners and referring veterinariansYour Working HoursIt is important to us that your working day can be planned reliably. Our laboratory is therefore organized in such a way that overtime is generally not required. Should overtime nevertheless arise, it will of course be compensated with time off. Electronic time tracking ensures transparency and reliable documentation of your working hours.The position can be filled on a part-time basis with 12 to 30 hours per week. If you are interested in additionally working in one of our other veterinary departments, we would also be happy to employ you on a full-time basis.If you would like to support us four days per week, you can take on more responsible and increasingly independent tasks in our laboratory, as these require a greater time commitment as well as a certain level of routine in the workflows.The position is particularly suitable for veterinarians who would like to combine their doctoral research at another institution with intensive practical experience in laboratory diagnostics. Through close collaboration with our medical team, you will also gain a comprehensive insight into clinical contexts and can specifically further develop your veterinary knowledge.Your working hours will be distributed evenly between early and late shifts. Early shifts start at 7:30 a.m., while late shifts end at 8:00 p.m. In addition, you will work at least one weekend per month from 11:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.Please state in your cover letter your possible working hours and when you would be available to start working with us.CompensationAs a veterinary clinic, our compensation is based on our veterinary remuneration structures. Please include your salary expectations in your cover letter.Would you like to learn more about us? Here you can find out (https://www.tierklinik-ismaning.de/ueber-die-tierklinik-ismaning/jobs/ihr-neuer-job/)  what distinguishes us as an employer and what employee benefits we offer.The position can be started immediately, or at a later date by agreement.
